title: Inclusions and finite equalities of compact opens descend in a spectral inverse limit
statement: Let I be a nonempty directed preordered set, (S_i) a system of spectral spaces with spectral transition maps f_{ij}, identities and composition laws. Let X be a space with compatible maps p_i and assume every compatible family of points has a unique point of X. Then (i) inclusion of two pulled-back quasi-compact opens descends to a common stage; (ii) finite union equalities of pulled-back quasi-compact opens descend to a stage; and (iii) finite intersection equalities descend to a stage.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0A30, parts (2)--(4), using Tag 0A2X for inclusion descent and formal finite union/intersection argument

proof.text: For two compact opens U_i and V_j whose pullbacks satisfy inclusion, pass to the directed upper tail above i and j. The differences of their pullbacks are closed in the constructible topologies and stable under transition maps. If all differences were nonempty, the compatible-point theorem for constructibly closed subsets would produce a compatible family, which extends to all indices and contradicts the assumed inclusion on X. Hence one difference is empty, giving inclusion at a common stage.

For a finite union or finite intersection family, combine the family into one compact open at the original stage. Apply inclusion descent in both directions and pass to a common upper bound; inverse images commute with unions and intersections. The empty family uses the empty or whole compact open as appropriate.
